data.narrative:
eGenesis is a Series C-stage biotech company in the Biotech & Health sector. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies, with direct stage-matched comps including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the company's $250M+ total raised, yielding $425M. Peer-median anchoring across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $3.8B, with a range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public comp anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of revenue data. The wide dispersion in peer valuations—particularly the $10.3B valuation of Colossal Biosciences relative to the $3.1B floor—reflects material heterogeneity in stage progression and underlying asset risk within the cohort.

Triangulating the two applicable methods yields a range of $361M to $4.4B, with a median of $2.1B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer medians dominate the midpoint. Key uncertainties include the degree to which eGenesis's scientific IP and IP position merit a premium or discount relative to the Colossal/Chai/New Limit tranche, and whether the $250M raised proxy adequately reflects pre-money momentum. The wide interquartile spread counsels caution regarding point estimates.
